memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And the pig, though it has a divided hoof, does not chew the cud; it is unclean for you. You must not eat their meat or touch their carcasses; they are unclean for you." - Lev 11:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The pig gets its own moment, and history has remembered it. Of all the animals in this chapter, this is the one that became a symbol — the sharpest boundary marker between Israel and the nations around them. Centuries later, when foreign rulers wanted to crush Jewish faith, this was the very point they pressed.

Notice the two-part command: do not eat, and do not touch the carcass. Uncleanness was not only about what went into the body. It could be caught by contact. A person could be going about a perfectly ordinary day and become ceremonially unclean simply by handling something dead.

That word — dead — is worth pausing on. Again and again in Leviticus, uncleanness clings to death. Death is the intruder in God's good world, the wage of sin (Rom 6:23), and everything it touches is marked by it. These laws taught Israel, in the language of daily life, that death and the holy God do not mix.

Then Jesus came. And here is the wonder: when He touched a leper, He was not made unclean — the leper was made clean (Mark 1:41-42). When He took a dead girl by the hand, life flowed the other way (Mark 5:41). At the cross He entered death itself, and death did not stain Him. It broke.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "boundary" has God drawn in your life that you find costly to keep?
2. How does it comfort you that Jesus was not contaminated by what He touched?
3. Where do you need Christ's cleansing touch today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You that instead of being defiled by what You touched, You made it clean. Touch the places in me that feel unclean, and make me whole by Your grace. Amen.
